pages.text: 10 mg/ml. Strong analgesia, an opioid: depresses breathing, especially with diazepam. Reversed by naloxone.
TXA, 1000 mg/ml: reduces bleeding, especially internal.
30 mg/ml: non-opioid analgesia. Overdose — more bleeding.
0.4 mg/ml: reverses opioids at once. Medicine 4.
5 mg/ml: sedation, drowsiness, lower pulse. With an opioid depresses breathing.
1 mg/ml: speeds up a slow pulse. Medicine 5.
10 IU/ml: lowers blood sugar (diabetes). Too much — hypoglycemia.
20 mg/ml, vial: local anesthesia of a body part — for sutures and surgery.
50 mg/ml, vial: anesthesia for a few minutes, keeps breathing. Medicine 7.
250 mg/ml, vial: injected antibiotic, stronger than pills. Medicine 5.
10 mg/ml, into a drip: anesthesia lasts while it drips; depresses breathing — intubate. Medicine 7.
1 mg/ml, into a drip: keeps blood pressure in shock. Medicine 6.
